interest: For historians of modern Japan and East Asian international relations, this file is particularly valuable as a record of U.S. State Department tracking of Japanese linguistic policy and cultural imperialism during the 1930s. It highlights the international dimension of Japan's domestic language controversies, notably the contentious debate over Romanization (Romaji) that culminated in the 1937 cabinet decree establishing the nationalist Kunrei-shiki system over the Hepburn system, including protests directed to the Prime Minister. Furthermore, the file documents the cultural and administrative instruments of Japanese imperial expansion on the Asian mainland, demonstrating how Japanese was imposed as a compulsory subject in primary schools in occupied Peiping in 1939 and how it rapidly supplanted English as the predominant language of commerce in Tsingtao.
overview: This file consists of the State Department's two-page 'List of Papers' (docket sheet) for decimal file 894.402, classified under 'Social Matters (Japan) - Language.' Covering entries and cross-references recorded between approximately 1910 and 1939, the register documents diplomatic and consular reporting on the Japanese language, orthography, and linguistic policies at home and abroad. Key subjects indexed include consular inquiries from Nagasaki regarding the necessity of accurately transcribing Japanese characters and Latin spellings for immigrant investigations; a report from Istanbul on a Japanese scholar studying Turkey's Latin alphabet revolution; the commercial displacement of English by Japanese in Tsingtao as reflected in local Chinese business commentary; the official 1937 promulgation by the Japanese government of a new Romanization system (Romaji) and subsequent domestic protests; and the mandated teaching of Japanese in primary schools in Japanese-occupied Peiping following the outbreak of the Second Sino-Japanese War.

subfiles.about: Two-page State Department List of Papers docket sheet indexing documents and cross-references filed under decimal file 894.402 regarding the Japanese language between 1910 and 1939.
subfiles.summary: This two-page docket sheet comprises the complete State Department 'List of Papers' register for decimal file 894.402 (Languages - Japan), cataloguing ten communications, reports, and cross-reference entries from 1910 through 1939. The register records early consular despatches from Nagasaki addressing the technical challenges of rendering Japanese characters and names for immigrant investigations, as well as a 1932 report from Istanbul on a Japanese scholar's study of the Turkish Latin alphabet revolution. In 1936 and 1937, the entries document the growing importance of the Japanese language over English in Tsingtao and detailed reports from the Tokyo Embassy on Japan's adoption of the new official Romanization (Romaji) system, complete with texts of cabinet decrees, syllabaries, and domestic letters of protest. The final entry from February 1939 cross-references a military attaché report on the compulsory instruction of the Japanese language in primary schools in Japanese-occupied Peiping.
subfiles.title: List of Papers for Decimal File 894.402: Languages - Japan
